According to Nepal's disaster response agency, more than 7,500 people have been rescued, nearly 2,500 are missing, and 219 people have been injured in the disaster. The tourism board earlier shared an update that 250 foreign nationals had been rescued, though 320 were still unaccounted for. To support the later part of that argument it often stresses its share in the global total of greenhouse gas emissions – the prime culprit of global warming -- which is less than 0.05%, according to some studies. With almost all its electricity generation from hydropower given its abundant water resources, much of them Himalayan glacier-fed, it has also been trying to ramp up installation of other clean energies like solar and wind. And then, officials say, it has protected more than 46% of its land as forests that are also carbon sinks – a major weapon in the world’s fight against climate crisis. Years of political instability has also meant that it has not been able to do what it could to adapt to some of the inevitable impacts of climate change. It has received significant climate finance from developed world and international financing agencies for adaptation over the years. Many of the bodies cannot be easily identified, but DNA samples will be collected and identifying marks recorded, with records kept, including about the location of burial, officials say. \"It has been decided to bury them systematically in government, community or forest areas, so that the bodies and remains can be given to those who come to search for them later,\" the spokesperson says.
